name: Architecture
description: Read the clues in stone, glass and steel to name the architectural style.
info: Photos: Wikimedia Commons, under CC BY-SA and other free licences; each photo's credit is shown with it.
question: Which architectural style?

cards.prompt: Pointed arches, ribbed vaults and flying buttresses let walls soar and fill with stained glass.
cards.fact: Gothic began in 12th-century France with Abbot Suger's rebuilding of the Basilica of Saint-Denis.

image.alt: Side of a tall stone cathedral lined with rows of pinnacled buttresses and arches

cards.prompt: Notre-Dame de Paris, with its great rose windows, gargoyles and flying buttresses.
cards.fact: After the 2019 fire, Notre-Dame reopened in December 2024.

image.alt: Twin-towered stone cathedral front with a round rose window and three carved portals
image.credit: DXR / Daniel Vorndran, via Wikimedia Commons

cards.prompt: Thick walls, small windows and heavy round arches give churches a solid, fortress-like feel.
cards.fact: Romanesque flourished in Europe from about 1000 to 1200; in England it is usually called "Norman."

image.alt: Stone abbey church with sturdy towers, thick walls, small round-arched windows
image.credit: CEphoto, Uwe Aranas, via Wikimedia Commons

cards.prompt: Pisa Cathedral and its famous leaning bell tower, wrapped in tiers of round-arched arcades.
cards.fact: The tower began leaning during construction in the 12th century because of soft ground.

image.alt: White marble cathedral with tiers of arcades beside a leaning round bell tower on a lawn
image.credit: José Luiz Bernardes Ribeiro, via Wikimedia Commons

cards.prompt: A vast central dome floats on pendentives above walls glittering with gold mosaics, as at Hagia Sophia.
cards.fact: Hagia Sophia was completed in 537 under Emperor Justinian.

image.alt: Huge domed building with smaller half-domes, flanked by four slender minarets

cards.prompt: St Mark's Basilica in Venice, crowned by five domes and lined with golden mosaics.
cards.fact: Its golden mosaics earned St Mark's the nickname "Chiesa d'Oro," Church of Gold.

image.alt: Ornate church front with golden mosaic arches, marble columns and domes behind

cards.prompt: Pointed arches, dazzling geometric tilework, honeycomb muqarnas vaults and a great courtyard with a pool.
cards.fact: Islamic art favors geometric and floral patterns, often avoiding images of people in religious spaces.

image.alt: Courtyard with a tall arched gateway and arcades covered in blue patterned tiles

cards.prompt: The Alhambra in Granada, with lace-like carved stucco and the Court of the Lions.
cards.fact: The Alhambra was the palace-fortress of the Nasrid dynasty, the last Muslim rulers in Spain.

image.alt: Palace courtyard ringed by slender columns and finely carved arches, with a fountain and cypress trees

cards.prompt: The Taj Mahal: gleaming white marble, a swelling onion dome, four minarets and mirrored gardens.
cards.fact: Emperor Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.

image.alt: White marble tomb with a bulbous central dome and four minarets, beyond a long garden pool
image.credit: © Yann Forget / Wikimedia Commons (edited by King of Hearts), via Wikimedia Commons

cards.prompt: Red sandstone inlaid with white marble, bulbous domes, kiosk-like chhatris and four-part charbagh gardens.
cards.fact: Humayun's Tomb in Delhi, begun in 1565, was an early inspiration for the Taj Mahal.

image.alt: Red sandstone tomb trimmed with white marble and a white dome, reflected in a garden pool

cards.prompt: A tower of stacked, tiered roofs with upturned eaves, often built to house Buddhist relics.
cards.fact: Pagodas descend from the Indian stupa, a dome-shaped Buddhist shrine.

image.alt: Wooden tower of five stacked roofs with upturned eaves and a tall bronze spire, among trees

cards.prompt: Hōryū-ji temple in Nara, Japan, with its slender five-story wooden tower.
cards.fact: Hōryū-ji holds some of the oldest surviving wooden buildings in the world.

image.alt: Slender dark wooden tower with five tiers of deep tiled roofs and a spire

cards.prompt: Symmetry, columns and harmonious domes revive ancient Roman proportions, as in Brunelleschi's dome in Florence.
cards.fact: Brunelleschi's dome, completed in 1436, was built without the usual wooden centering frame.

image.alt: Great red-tiled dome with white ribs rising above a city at dusk, hills behind

cards.prompt: Palladio's Villa La Rotonda: a square villa with a temple-front portico on each of its four sides.
cards.fact: Palladio's villas inspired countless later buildings, including Thomas Jefferson's Monticello.

image.alt: Symmetrical villa with a columned temple-front portico, broad steps and a low dome

cards.prompt: Dramatic curves, a soaring dome, giant sculpted columns and theatrical light and shadow, as at Vienna's Karlskirche.
cards.fact: Baroque arose in Rome around 1600, partly to inspire awe during the Counter-Reformation.

image.alt: Floodlit church with a tall oval dome, curving wings and two giant sculpted columns

cards.prompt: Bernini's sweeping colonnade of columns embracing St Peter's Square in Rome.
cards.fact: Bernini said the curving arms represent the Church embracing the faithful.

image.alt: Vast square embraced by a curving colonnade of columns topped with statues, an obelisk at center

cards.prompt: The Palace of Versailles, with its glittering Hall of Mirrors and vast formal gardens.
cards.fact: The Hall of Mirrors holds 357 mirrors and hosted the signing of the Treaty of Versailles in 1919.

image.alt: Long, grand palace facade seen across a formal garden fountain with a bronze statue
image.credit: King of Hearts, via Wikimedia Commons

cards.prompt: A Greek-temple front with tall columns and a triangular pediment, as on the U.S. Capitol.
cards.fact: Neoclassicism spread in the 1700s after excavations at Pompeii revived interest in antiquity.

image.alt: White government building with a columned central front and a large dome on a drum
image.credit: Architect of the Capitol (derivative work: O.J.), via Wikimedia Commons

cards.prompt: Berlin's Brandenburg Gate, modeled on the monumental gateway to the Athenian Acropolis.
cards.fact: Completed in 1791, the gate is topped by a chariot drawn by four horses, the Quadriga.

image.alt: Monumental stone gateway of tall columns crowned by a statue of a horse-drawn chariot
image.credit: Thomas Wolf, www.foto-tw.de, via Wikimedia Commons

cards.prompt: Symmetrical red-brick townhouses with sash windows and a paneled front door crowned by a fanlight.
cards.fact: Georgian style is named for Britain's four King Georges, who reigned from 1714 to 1830.

image.alt: Row of symmetrical brick townhouses with tall sash windows and a red front door

cards.prompt: The Royal Crescent in Bath: a sweeping arc of 30 terraced houses behind a row of Ionic columns.
cards.fact: The Royal Crescent was built 1767–1774 by architect John Wood the Younger.

image.alt: Sweeping curved terrace of honey-colored stone houses fronted by a long row of columns
image.credit: Photograph by Mike Peel (www.mikepeel.net), via Wikimedia Commons

cards.prompt: Half-timbered walls of dark oak beams and white plaster, steep gables and tall clustered chimneys.
cards.fact: The Tudor period ran from 1485 to 1603, from Henry VII to Elizabeth I.

image.alt: Crooked half-timbered manor house with black beams, white panels and gables, behind a lawn
image.credit: Photograph by Mike Peel (www.mikepeel.net), via Wikimedia Commons

cards.prompt: The original red-brick wings of Hampton Court Palace, built for Cardinal Wolsey and seized by Henry VIII.
cards.fact: Henry VIII's great kitchens at Hampton Court could feed hundreds of courtiers a day.

image.alt: Red-brick palace gatehouse with battlemented turrets and a large oriel window over the arch
image.credit: Steve Cadman from London, U.K., via Wikimedia Commons

cards.prompt: Ornate gingerbread trim, bay windows, turrets and bright paint, like San Francisco's "Painted Ladies."
cards.fact: Victorian style is named for Queen Victoria, who reigned from 1837 to 1901.

image.alt: Row of colorful wooden houses with bay windows and gables in front of a city skyline
image.credit: King of Hearts / Wikimedia Commons / CC-BY-SA-3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

cards.prompt: Whiplash curves inspired by plants, in wrought iron and glass, like Hector Guimard's Paris Métro entrances.
cards.fact: Art Nouveau, "new art," flourished from about 1890 to 1910.

image.alt: Subway entrance with a fan-shaped glass canopy on curving green iron supports

cards.prompt: Gaudí's Casa Batlló in Barcelona, with bone-like balconies and a rippling roof of scale-like tiles.
cards.fact: Locals nicknamed Casa Batlló the "House of Bones."

image.alt: Townhouse with a wavy mosaic facade, bone-like balconies and a scaly, humped roof

cards.prompt: Bold geometric zigzags, sunbursts and a stepped, gleaming steel spire, as on New York's Chrysler Building.
cards.fact: Completed in 1930, the Chrysler Building was briefly the world's tallest building.

image.alt: Skyscraper crown of stacked steel arches with triangular windows, tapering to a needle spire

cards.prompt: Pastel facades with porthole windows, racing stripes and neon trim along Miami Beach's Ocean Drive.
cards.fact: Miami Beach's Art Deco district was listed on the U.S. National Register of Historic Places in 1979.

image.alt: Seafront street of pastel low-rise hotels with rounded corners and palm trees

cards.prompt: Flat roofs, white cubic blocks and bands of windows from the German design school founded by Walter Gropius.
cards.fact: The Bauhaus school opened in Weimar in 1919 and was forced to close by the Nazis in 1933.

image.alt: White flat-roofed blocks with a glass-walled wing and a tower of small balconies

cards.prompt: Glass curtain walls on a steel frame with no ornament at all: "less is more."
cards.fact: "Less is more" is the motto of architect Ludwig Mies van der Rohe.

image.alt: Dark, plain glass-and-steel office tower set back on a plaza between other high-rises
image.credit: Ken OHYAMA from FUNABASHI, Japan, via Wikimedia Commons

cards.prompt: A Le Corbusier house in Stuttgart's Weissenhof Estate: a white box on slender pillars with ribbon windows and a roof terrace.
cards.fact: Le Corbusier called a house "a machine for living in."

image.alt: White boxy house raised on thin pillars, with long horizontal windows and a roof terrace

cards.prompt: Massive, blocky buildings of raw, unpainted concrete with a fortress-like look.
cards.fact: The name comes from the French "béton brut," meaning raw concrete.

image.alt: Massive top-heavy building of raw concrete with deep, repetitive window fins over a brick plaza

cards.prompt: London's Barbican Estate: rough concrete towers, terraces and high walkways.
cards.fact: The Barbican was built on a site heavily bombed during the Blitz in World War II.

image.alt: Rough concrete walkway and housing blocks with a tall tower behind, beside a lawn

cards.prompt: Playful, ironic mixes of classical motifs and bright colors, like a skyscraper topped by a giant broken pediment.
cards.fact: Architect Robert Venturi answered "less is more" with a joke: "Less is a bore."

image.alt: Pink granite skyscraper topped by a triangular pediment split by a round notch
image.credit: David Shankbone (cropped by Beyond My Ken), via Wikimedia Commons

cards.prompt: Fragmented, tilting forms and swooping titanium curves, as at Frank Gehry's Guggenheim Bilbao.
cards.fact: The Guggenheim Bilbao opened in 1997 and helped revive the city's economy.

image.alt: Museum of swirling, tilted metal-clad curves on a riverbank beside a bridge
image.credit: José Ligero Loarte, via Wikimedia Commons
